iskaypet.title: At Iskaypet 🐾
iskaypet.intro: I dove headfirst into the ecommerce world, working on the Tiendanimal and Kiwoko websites, which are built on Salesforce. But we're continuing to advance. We're on a mission to migrate everything to Headless using Next.js, and as the team's Next.js lead, I'm leading the charge on research, standardization, and setting up the foundational projects for this epic journey.
iskaypet.ecommerce: Here, I work with Salesforce, Jquery, JavaScript, and Sass. A real tech cocktail!
iskaypet.componentLibraryTitle: Component Library for Tiendanimal's Design System:
iskaypet.componentLibrary: Built this one from scratch, using React, Rollup, and Sass. Also threw in lint, jest, stylelint, and Vitest to keep things neat.
iskaypet.ssrProject: We worked on the migration from Salesforce to Next.js using TypeScript, Zod, Sass, and tRPC. We established the initial foundations, including all basics and full observability with Grafana Faro, traces, and error logs, creating base dashboards. Subsequently, we created the first headless page for the 'My Orders' section, which was a complete success, featuring robust error control, full visibility, and excellent compatibility with other headless pages, authentication, common components, styles, etc.

cloudappi.title: Cloudappi Adventures 🌩️
cloudappi.intro: At Cloudappi, I became a tech specialist, creating web apps with VUE 3, Angular, and .NET Core. We were all about that SCRUM life, and I got to use powerful tools like GitLab, Redmine, Odoo, and Jira. Whether it was a big project or a small one, I was there, adding value with Bootstrap, Buefy, and Bulma, and of course, making sure everything was tip-top with e2e and unit tests.
cloudappi.simulationTitle: Simulation for Pre-Offers with a Map:
cloudappi.simulation: Got to work with Vue 3, Bulma, and TypeScript. It was like building a treasure map, but for installations!
cloudappi.mapManagement: This one was all about Blazor and Bootstrap. Like a cartographer, but for data!
cloudappi.listing: Dived into Angular and TypeScript for this one. It was like being a librarian, but for data!
